predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of US ground forces entering Gaza signals changing Middle East conflict dynamics. The directional effect on oil is genuinely ambiguous: direct US military involvement could mean escalation (risk premium up) OR a stabilization/ceasefire enforcement role (de-escalation, premium down). Gaza itself is not an oil producer, so transmission runs only through broader regional-conflict and Iran/Hormuz spillover risk, which is diffuse. Over a 12h window the link to a 700bps move is very unlikely.

predictions.reasoning: Higher odds of US boots on the ground in Gaza imply increased US military operational tempo and potential procurement, a mild tailwind for defense primes. But the exclusions (contractors, advisors, special forces, diplomatic entourage don't count) narrow the trigger to a large-footprint regular deployment, which is a low-probability tail event. Defense names are also driven far more by budget cycles and existing conflicts than a single Gaza-deployment probability tick, so expected 12h move is small.

llm_justification.summary: This market tracks a low-probability, narrowly-defined tail event (US regular ground troops physically in Gaza) over a multi-year horizon, making its 12h public-market signal weak and ambiguous. The most plausible proxies are crude oil (via Middle East risk premium, but direction is two-sided between escalation and stabilization) and US defense equities (mild upside bias). Both mappings are low-confidence and well below the 700bps tradable threshold; this is a noisy sensor best treated as non-tradable.
key_assumptions: A sharp implied-probability move reflects new information about US-Gaza force posture rather than market noise
Oil responds to Middle East escalation/de-escalation risk premium
Defense equities get a mild bid from higher US operational-tempo expectations
failure_modes: The probability move is noise or reflects already-public reporting, so assets don't react
Oil direction is wrong because the event is de-escalatory (stabilization force) rather than escalatory
Gaza has no direct commodity exposure; the oil proxy is only weakly linked
Defense ETF is dominated by budget/other-conflict drivers, so this specific catalyst is immaterial
The strict resolution exclusions mean the market can move without any real-world deployment that would move assets
